acceptanceCriteria: The system displays the promo code discount amount for the return trip line item in the Mozio email confirmation when a promo code is applied to a return trip order.
The system displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound trip and the return trip line items in the Mozio email confirmation when a promo code is applied to a return trip order.

The system calculates the promo code discount amount for the return trip using the same discount logic applied to the outbound trip, ensuring the displayed amounts are consistent with the order's total discount.

The system displays the promo code discount amount as zero or omits the promo code line for the return trip when no promo code is applied to the order, without causing a rendering error in the email confirmation.
The system correctly renders the promo code discount amount for the return trip when the return trip line item has a different station pair (reversed from/to) than the outbound trip line item.

The system handles the case where the promo code discount applies to only one leg of a return trip by displaying the discount amount only on the applicable leg and showing zero or no promo line on the other leg, without misrepresenting the total discount.

The system includes the promo code discount amount for the return trip in the email confirmation regardless of the product code or passenger type (e.g., senior, adult) associated with the return trip line item.

The system logs an error and still sends the email confirmation with the outbound trip promo discount displayed when the return trip promo discount calculation fails, ensuring the customer receives a confirmation email without a complete failure.

acceptanceCriteria: Given a return trip dispatch where report.price.discount.amount.value = X and discount.name = 'PROMO10', the sanitized dispatch output contains discount.amount.value = X and discount.name = '<masked>' — identical structure and values as an outbound dispatch with the same discount input.

Given a return trip order with a promo code discount of $D applied to a line item with quantity Q, the dispatch report.price.discount.amount.value equals the sum of all discount contributions from line items belonging to that dispatch, and report.price.discount.name contains the promo code identifier.

Given a promo code applied to a return trip order where both legs share the discount, each dispatch's report.price.discount.amount.value > 0, and the sum of both dispatches' discount.amount.value equals the total order-level discount amount.

Given a return trip order with no promo code applied, the return trip dispatch report.price.discount is undefined, and the sanitized dispatch output omits the discount field entirely — no empty or zero-valued discount object is emitted.

Given a promo code discount that applies to only the outbound leg of a return trip, the outbound dispatch report.price.discount.amount.value equals the discount amount for that leg, and the return dispatch report.price.discount is undefined — the total discount is not split or duplicated across legs.

Given a return trip order with a promo code discount and line items of varying passenger types (e.g., senior, adult), each line item's discount contribution equals (discount per unit × quantity), and the dispatch report.price.discount.amount.value equals the sum of those contributions — the result is independent of passenger type or product code.

Given a return trip discount calculation that throws an error, the system logs the error and the email confirmation is still sent with the outbound dispatch discount displayed — the customer receives a confirmation without a complete failure.
after.description: The promo code discount amount is not displayed correctly for return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The root cause is in how the discount is calculated and mapped for return trip dispatches — the discount amount is either missing or miscalculated on the return trip dispatch's report.price.discount before it reaches the email rendering path.

notes: Added 3 new ACs and modified 1 existing AC. AC7 was modified to make 'logs the error' more observable by specifying that the error is captured in error records with identifying detail, rather than the vague 'the system logs the error'. Added AC8 to verify the end-user-visible outcome — the email confirmation actually displays the discount amount, which is the core bug described in the story title but was not covered by any existing AC (all existing ACs only verified the dispatch data layer). Added AC9 to cover rounding/precision edge cases when fractional discount values are split across legs, preventing floating-point drift. Added AC10 to cover malformed discount data (null/undefined amount.value) ensuring no partially-constructed discount objects leak into dispatches.
